findings.title: Census update for the MegaETH forced exit limit: 38 of 138 positions need a new fee growth slot on their next update
findings.difference: MegaETH prices a first write to a slot by the size of its SALT bucket, which any account can grow, and its L1 portal rejects a deposit above 1,000,000 gas. This cycle only refreshes the count of exposed positions.
findings.mechanism: Position.update stores both fee growth inside values on every liquidity change without a condition (src/libraries/Position.sol:77-108). A position whose stored value is zero and whose current inside growth is nonzero must therefore write a new nonzero slot on its next update, removal included. Reading every ModifyLiquidity log of the PoolManager from block 7,009,653 to 33,040,742 (1,360 logs, 292 positions) gives 138 positions with net liquidity, and the position slot equals the log sum for all 138. For each, the stored last values and the current inside growth were read with eth_getStorageAt and computed as getFeeGrowthInside does (src/libraries/Pool.sol:488-511). 38 positions in 17 of 102 pools need at least one new slot and 30 of them need two. 21 of the 38 belong to the PositionManager 0x9ae0921e981aaa7308f176f8d4f9129b9247c89d and 15 to 0x5f16b71cc05b146d73e181354b1c8ac89fc4bbc3. The other writes of a removal can be avoided by the remover: the recipient's first token balance by taking to an address that already holds the token, and a first ERC-6909 balance by taking instead of minting (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297 and 322-328). The fee growth write cannot be avoided. The rest of the mechanism is as F-105 records: the bucket growth and the portal cap need the sequencer to refuse the provider before they matter.
findings.impact: Only positions whose holders lose sequencer access are affected, and only for their L1 exit. The eight pools with the most liquidity hold none of the 38 positions. The dollar share was not computed, because it needs prices for 17 pools.
findings.preconditions: An account grows the buckets of the target slots, and the sequencer refuses or stops including the provider's transactions.
findings.mitigations: A provider can update the position once through the sequencer (for example a zero-liquidity poke after fees accrue) so the fee growth slots are nonzero before any exit is needed.

cleared.check: Lead L-1340: can block 0xde6 of the compiled PoolManager (the delta read of clear) run its out-of-line CALLDATALOAD path, which serves calldata shorter than offset 0x24 plus 32 bytes, that is shorter than 68 bytes, including calldata of exactly 4, 35 and 36 bytes?
cleared.result: No. In the deployed bytecode (24,009 bytes, sha256 288b97729c9e4f34..., equal to eth_getCode on rpc.monad.xyz on 2026-11-28) the selector 0x80f0b44c jumps to 0xd87, which reverts at 0xdb6 to 0x330 when calldatasize minus 4 is less than 64 (signed). It then calls the address check at 0x2d3f, returns to 0xdbe, checks the unlock flag, and falls through to 0xde6. 0xde6 is not a JUMPDEST and the only PUSH2 of 0x0dbe in the code is at 0xdb7, so every entry to 0xde6 has calldata of at least 68 bytes and CALLDATALOAD(0x24) never takes the short path. Live eth_call of clear with 35, 36 and 67 bytes reverts with empty data on both networks (and with 4 bytes on MegaETH), and with 68 bytes reverts with ManagerLocked 0x54e3ca0d, so the decoder check runs before the lock check. The amount compared at src/PoolManager.sol:314 is always read from calldata in bounds.

cleared.check: Lead L-1334: is there a public method on mainnet.megaeth.com whose answer comes from the sequencer's JIT rather than a replica, other than transaction submission?
cleared.result: No. The RPC reference fetched on 2026-11-28 lists eth_call, eth_callMany, eth_createAccessList and eth_estimateGas as routed to the compute pool, and debug_traceCall, eth_callAfter and trace_call as unavailable. rpc_modules, realtime_call, mega_call, eth_callBundle, eth_simulateV1 and debug_traceCall return -32601 on the endpoint. Only eth_sendRawTransactionSync and realtime_sendRawTransaction return the sequencer's result, and they need a real transaction. The F-166 vectors therefore cannot be run against the producer through a read-only call. This repeats the cycle 19 result with today's page.

leads.question: Which build and version do the Monad RPC providers run that the v0.16.7 announcement calls the recent hotfix, and does it change eth_call execution or only RPC handling?
leads.why: Public evidence on Monad comes from eth_call. A provider that answers from an unpublished hotfix build could disagree with validators without anyone seeing it.

leadResults.answer: The short-calldata path of CALLDATALOAD(0x24) in block 0xde6 cannot run. The ABI decoder at 0xd8d to 0xdb6 reverts when calldatasize minus 4 is less than 64 before control reaches 0xde6. 0xde6 is entered only by falling through from 0xdbe, and 0xdbe is pushed only at 0xdb7. Live eth_call on Monad and MegaETH confirms it: 35, 36 and 67 bytes revert with empty data and 68 bytes reverts with ManagerLocked. The 4 byte call was rate limited on Monad and reverts with empty data on MegaETH. The path is dead code for this block, so it cannot change the amount compared at src/PoolManager.sol:314.

At block 33,040,742 MegaETH has 138 positions with liquidity. Their slot liquidity equals the log sum in all 138. 38 positions in 17 of 102 pools must write at least one new fee growth slot on their next update, and 30 must write two. 21 of the 38 belong to the PositionManager and 15 to 0x5f16b71c. The fee growth write is the only new PoolManager slot a removal cannot avoid (src/libraries/Position.sol:99-100). The remover controls the recipient's token slot and the ERC-6909 slot. None of the 38 is in the eight pools with the most liquidity. The dollar share was not computed. The hazard stays operator-only (F-105).

No public read-only method reaches the sequencer. The RPC reference fetched on 2026-11-28 routes eth_call, eth_callMany, eth_createAccessList and eth_estimateGas to the compute pool and lists debug_traceCall, trace_call and eth_callAfter as unavailable; the endpoint returns -32601 for rpc_modules, realtime_call, mega_call, eth_callBundle, eth_simulateV1 and debug_traceCall. Only transaction submission returns the producer's result, and this review may not send transactions. The F-166 vectors cannot be run on the JIT.

Operator-only. mega-reth is closed, so its megaeth-labs/revm tag cannot be read. The public mega-evm v1.7.4, also main on 2026-11-28, pins crates.io revm =40.0.3 with no patch to the fork (Cargo.toml line 141), the same as the stateless validator. The fork's baseline is still v112 (scripts/mega/base.txt on main).
